cohort_disposition_reason: 5 of 6 runguide Cohort A targets are web-only products with no desktop installer; 1 is Microsoft-Store-distributed UWP (not Electron). No Cohort A binary actionable as written.

per_vendor_absence_rows.verification: Vendor documentation explicitly states users access Command via web browser; no desktop client distributed.

Eagle Eye Viewer is distributed via Microsoft Store as a UWP (.msix), not as an Electron .exe. Distribution model mismatches Cohort A Electron tooling. Could be re-scoped to a separate UWP cohort in a follow-on wave.
Rhombus Console is cloud-only at console.rhombussystems.com; no desktop installer distributed. WebCatalog/BlueStacks third-party wrappers exist but are not vendor-distributed.

Avigilon Alta product line is cloud-based; Alta Aware analytics surfaces via web. The 'Avigilon ACC Client' that does have a desktop installer is the legacy on-prem VMS (Cohort C native, not Cohort A Electron — already separately listed in runguide §3.1 Cohort C).

Skydio Pilot is iOS/Android mobile app + web portal. No Electron desktop client distributed despite runguide's '(web bundle, downloadable as Electron)' framing. Runguide author acknowledged uncertainty at framing-time; substantive premise verifies as absent.

Verkada Command Connector is a hardware appliance product (gateway/bridge); not distributed as desktop software. May ship firmware images potentially fitting Cohort E if Verkada distributes them publicly, but that is a Cohort E rescope.

cp17_cohort_thesis_finding.thesis_under_test: Wave G mobile operator-vs-installer cohort thesis (CP17 §8.2 vendor-app identifier sub-band ladder) generalizes from mobile to desktop.
cp17_cohort_thesis_finding.preliminary_finding_from_cohort_a_probe: The 'operator-cohort desktop' class is largely absent in the modern VMS landscape. Vendors have moved operator workflows to web-first / mobile-first architectures, eliminating the standalone desktop client for operator use cases. The 'installer-cohort desktop' class persists (Cohorts B .NET, C native C++) because installer/admin workflows need rich UI surface that web cannot match.
cp17_cohort_thesis_finding.thesis_disposition: Partial generalization. Installer-cohort half of CP17 carries from mobile to desktop. Operator-cohort half does NOT generalize — operator-cohort dissolves into web/mobile rather than appearing as a separate desktop class. This is a one-sided generalization, not a clean carry-over.
cp17_cohort_thesis_finding.policy_implication: Lynceus / Talos consumers should treat Wave H findings as installer-cohort-weighted (Cohorts B/C/D/F). Lack of operator-cohort desktop class is itself a finding worth codifying — it suggests vendor architectural shift in the 2020-2026 window away from desktop operator clients.
cp17_cohort_thesis_finding.cp28_candidate_note: If Lynceus needs to filter operator-cohort findings, the absence of an operator-cohort desktop class means the Wave G mobile operator-cohort remains the primary surface. No CP28 follow-up needed on this axis until cross-vendor sample is larger.

next_cohort_dispatch: Cohort B (.NET / WPF VMS clients) — highest expected yield with confirmed public-download targets (Milestone via self-issue, plus Genetec / Lenel / Honeywell / Tyco / Gallagher trials).
